Rivers deliver to estuaries and coastal waters the nutrients, sediment and
freshwater released by their catchment. Here, we ask how the land use and
climate of the catchment shape the fish communities of estuaries and coastal
bays, in the four districts of interest. It builds on the environmental
gradient of D19: stressors are added on top of the continuum variables
selected there.

**Hypotheses.** Fish are grouped by their use of estuaries (guilds, see D19).

| Driver | Expected change | Expected effect on the communities |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Farmland (arable) | More nitrate and phosphate exported; more fine sediment and turbidity | Moderate enrichment raises the productivity of nurseries: more marine juveniles (flatfish, sea bass); strong enrichment brings algal blooms and hypoxia: fewer sensitive estuarine residents and marine juveniles |
| Urban areas | More ammonium, organic matter and contaminants | Fewer marine juveniles and sensitive residents, more tolerant species |
| Rainfall of the year, catchment size | More freshwater: lower salinity, more nutrients delivered | More freshwater and diadromous species, fewer marine stragglers; higher nursery production of sole in wet years |
| Temperature (catchment and year) | Warmer water; with nutrients, more hypoxia | More warm-water marine species and residents, fewer cold-water species (plaice, whiting, smelt, flounder) |

## Setup

```{r setup}
library(renv)
renv::load()
library(targets)
library(here)
tar_config_set(
  store = here::here("_targets")
)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
devtools::load_all()
nice_theme()
```

```{r data}
operation <- tar_read(sea_operation)
france <- rnaturalearth::ne_countries(scale = "medium", country = "France", returnclass = "sf")
```

## Catchment of each estuary

Each operation is linked to the main river flowing into its estuary or
bay, and related to the land use of that river's catchment. Small streams
entering the same estuary (e.g. the marsh channels along the Gironde) are
merged with its main river: the water of the estuary comes mostly from
it.

- **Main rivers:** the AMOBIO river mouths (as in D8) draining 1,000 km²
  or more; mouths closer than 3 km are pooled (e.g. the Orne and the Dan
  at Caen).
- **Catchments:** computed on the HydroSHEDS flow directions (~400 m, as
  in D15). Each grid outlet takes the main river its stream reaches along
  the AMOBIO network: e.g. the Garonne and the Dordogne, which end at the
  head of the Gironde on the grid. Land cover and weather are read from
  the cached catchment rasters of D15.
- **Operations:** inland (upper estuaries), the main river reached along
  the network; at sea, the nearest main river mouth along the sea (D8),
  if within 15 km. The other operations are dropped. By hand: the
  operations of the Gironde estuary belong to the Gironde (the AMOBIO
  Gironde ends at its head, 20 to 70 km from them).

Targets: `main_mouth`, `network_mouth`, `mouth_outlet`,
`sea_operation_mouth`, `mouth_catchment`.

```{r mouth}
mouth <- tar_read(sea_mouth_area)
basin <- tar_read(mouth_basin)
operation_mouth <- operation |>
  select(operation_id, survey, district, longitude, latitude) |>
  left_join(tar_read(sea_operation_mouth), by = "operation_id")
mouth_used <- mouth |>
  filter(mouth_id %in% operation_mouth$mouth_id) |>
  arrange(district, desc(latitude))
palette_mouth <- c("#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#009E73", "#D55E00", "#0072B2", "#CC79A7", "#8C6D31")
colour_mouth <- setNames(rep_len(palette_mouth, nrow(mouth_used)), mouth_used$mouth_id)
```

```{r mouth-catchment}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-cap: "Catchments of the main rivers with operations (one colour per river), and the operations kept (black) or dropped (grey, more than 15 km from a main river mouth at sea)."

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = france, fill = "grey95", color = "grey70", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = factor(mouth_id)), data = filter(basin, mouth_id %in% mouth_used$mouth_id), color = "white", linewidth = 0.1, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_point(aes(longitude, latitude), data = filter(operation_mouth, is.na(mouth_id)), size = 0.2, color = "grey55") +
  geom_point(aes(longitude, latitude), data = filter(operation_mouth, !is.na(mouth_id)), size = 0.2) +
  ggrepel::geom_label_repel(
    aes(longitude, latitude, label = river), data = mouth_used,
    size = 2.6, label.size = 0.1, label.padding = 0.15, min.segment.length = 0, segment.size = 0.2, seed = 1
  ) +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(-5.2, 6), ylim = c(43, 51.2)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = colour_mouth, guide = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(axis.line = element_blank(), axis.text = element_text(size = 7))
```

```{r mouth-operation}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 13
#| fig-cap: "Operations coloured by their main river (triangle: mouth), per district; grey: dropped."

map_district <- \(d) {
  op <- filter(operation_mouth, district == d)
  m <- filter(mouth_used, mouth_id %in% op$mouth_id)
  ggplot() +
    geom_sf(data = france, fill = "grey95", color = "grey70", linewidth = 0.2) +
    geom_point(aes(longitude, latitude), data = filter(op, is.na(mouth_id)), size = 0.4, color = "grey70") +
    geom_point(aes(longitude, latitude, color = factor(mouth_id)), data = filter(op, !is.na(mouth_id)), size = 0.5, alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_point(aes(longitude, latitude, color = factor(mouth_id)), data = m, shape = 17, size = 2.4) +
    ggrepel::geom_text_repel(
      aes(longitude, latitude, label = river, color = factor(mouth_id)), data = m,
      size = 2.8, fontface = "bold", bg.color = "white", bg.r = 0.15,
      min.segment.length = 0, segment.size = 0.2, max.overlaps = Inf, seed = 1
    ) +
    coord_sf(xlim = range(op$longitude) + c(-0.1, 0.1), ylim = range(op$latitude) + c(-0.1, 0.1)) +
    scale_color_manual(values = colour_mouth, guide = "none") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = d) +
    theme(axis.line = element_blank(), axis.text = element_text(size = 7))
}
row_north <- patchwork::wrap_plots(map_district("Escaut-Somme"), map_district("Seine"), widths = c(1, 2.5))
row_south <- patchwork::wrap_plots(map_district("Loire"), map_district("Ardour-Garonne"), widths = c(2, 1))
patchwork::wrap_plots(row_north, row_south, ncol = 1, heights = c(1, 2))
```

```{r mouth-table}
operation_mouth |>
  filter(!is.na(mouth_id)) |>
  count(mouth_id, survey) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = survey, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  inner_join(mouth, by = "mouth_id") |>
  arrange(desc(area)) |>
  transmute(
    River = river, District = district, `POMET operations` = pomet,
    `Nursery survey operations` = nurse, `Catchment (km²)` = round(area)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

**Results:**

- `r nrow(mouth_used)` main rivers, from about 1,000 km² (Laïta, Rance)
  to 118,000 km² (Loire), with the large rivers at their known size
  (Gironde 82,000 km², Seine 76,000, Vilaine 10,500).
- `r format(sum(!is.na(operation_mouth$mouth_id)), big.mark = ",")` of
  `r format(nrow(operation_mouth), big.mark = ",")` operations are kept:
  most POMET operations (estuaries) but few nursery survey operations
  (bays away from the main mouths).

*To discuss:*

- Land use varies only between the `r nrow(mouth_used)` rivers, so its
  effects rest on few units.
- The bays dropped here could be added back with a land use exposure
  summing the main rivers nearby, weighted by distance at sea.

## Next steps

- Models of the communities against the catchment of their mouth, on top
  of the continuum variables of D19.
